nameOrigin.text: Investors from Holland bought the Caribou Mill in 1873 and renamed the town Nederland, which means lowland; it sits on lower ground than Caribou.

founded.text: Began as a huddle of cabins called Dayton

timeline.text: The town began as a huddle of cabins called Dayton, later known as Brown's Crossing.
Nederland resident Scott Harrison trucked the empty frame of a Looff carousel from Utah to Nederland and began carving animals for it.
The Carousel of Happiness opened on Memorial Day.
Boulder County bought the artifact collection of the Nederland Mining Museum, which the Nederland Area Historical Society had created and run.

sites.name: Carousel of Happiness
sites.hours: Days and times vary by season: generally 7 days a week from Memorial Day through Labor Day, weekends the rest of the year
sites.cost: $3 per ride; infants younger than 9 months ride free

trails.name: Hessie Trailhead and the Indian Peaks lakes
trails.manager: USDA Forest Service; Boulder County runs the access road and the summer shuttle
trails.length: Round trips from the trailhead: Lost Lake 4.2 miles, Woodland Lake 9.6, Devils Thumb 11.6, King Lake 12, Diamond Lake 13
trails.trailhead: From Nederland, 0.6 mile south on Colorado 119, then west on County Road 130 through the Town of Eldora; the left fork 0.75 mile past the end of the pavement. Parking is limited
trails.season: In winter, access is usually from the Town of Eldora; Boulder County’s summer shuttle returns Memorial Day weekend 2027.
trails.dogs: On a hand-held leash at all times.
trails.fee: No day-use fee for individuals; organized groups need a free day-hiking permit, and overnight trips June 1 to September 15 need a $5 permit.

trails.name: Brainard Lake Recreation Area
trails.length: Brainard Gateway Trailhead is 2.5 miles up Brainard Lake Road from Colorado 72 at Ward, and the lake two miles beyond it
trails.trailhead: Brainard Gateway Trailhead, on Brainard Lake Road west of Ward
trails.season: The gate at the Gateway Trailhead is open from about mid-June to mid-October; in winter, park at the Gateway for the ski and snowshoe trails.
trails.dogs: May 1 to November 14, on a hand-held leash; November 15 to April 30, only on the Brainard Lake and Lefthand Park Reservoir roads and the Sourdough Trail.
trails.fee: A $10 day-use fee from the Gateway Trailhead, no reservation; parking inside the area in summer needs a timed-entry reservation.
